raw_response:
I farm only 5 mu, so I cannot afford to gamble. We do wheat and then maize right after, same as most people here. I have done this for many years, and with some family members working off-farm, I need a plan that is steady and not too labor-heavy. Wheat is the main crop I watch closely because if wheat is weak, the whole year feels tight. I will sow winter wheat in early October with a common improved variety that people around here use, not the most expensive seed. I usually put base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once when the wheat starts growing fast in spring. If the year is dry, I will irrigate around sowing, jointing, and grain filling, but I will not irrigate too many times because pumping from the well costs money. For maize, the planting window is short after wheat harvest, so I will keep it simple: harvest wheat, clear the field quickly, and plant summer maize within a few days. I will use hybrid maize seed because the yield is more reliable. I will apply fertilizer mainly at planting and then one more time when the maize is growing strongly. If rain is decent, I may only irrigate once, but if it turns dry, I will give another watering around tasseling. I do not like to cut fertilizer too much because if the crop turns yellow, the yield loss is worse than saving a little cash. But I also cannot spend too much up front, so I stay close to what worked for me last year and what neighbors around me are doing.
